extractedText: Korean Cosmetics Stocks Slide 20% in Two Weeks, but Analysts See Buying WindowFinance|Published 2026.09.13. 10:00:48|By Nam Yoon-jungyjnam@sedaily.com|Summary|SaveAAAClipart KoreaKorean cosmetics stocks, which rallied through July and August, have retreated across the board in September. Brokerages say the sector could attempt a rebound ahead of the year-end shopping season, provided the won does not strengthen further.APR (278470), the largest cosmetics stock by market value, fell 19.91% this month through the previous session, according to the Korea Exchange on the 13th. That marks a sharp reversal from August, when the stock gained 45.16%.Silicon2 also dropped 19.74% this month after surging 59.65% in August. LG H&H (051900) and Amorepacific (090430) fell 7.03% and 4.55%, respectively, in September alone. Original design manufacturers were not spared either, with Cosmecca Korea down 16.09%, Kolmar Korea down 11.74% and Cosmax down 9.83%.Behind the declines were a combination of distorted export data and a stronger won. Average daily cosmetics exports came to $34.12 million during the first 10 days of last month, but a unit error is believed to have occurred in the figures for Canada. Excluding that, actual exports fall to about $25 million. The error was not corrected by month-end, prompting observations that it could show up as a reverse base effect in September export statistics.The won-dollar exchange rate has also fallen from the 1,430 range in early August to the 1,340 range now, reducing the won value of overseas dollar revenue. Some analysts say a 5% drop in the won-dollar rate could lower operating margins in the cosmetics sector by 0.7 to 0.8 percentage points.Brokerages, however, largely view the pullback as a buying opportunity. Analysts said share-price corrections in the cosmetics sector have always been buying opportunities, and projected that stocks would rebound quickly from October ahead of the fourth-quarter shopping season, as long as the won does not enter a sustained uptrend.Last year, Ulta Beauty ran an "Early Black Friday" promotion starting Oct. 26, while Amazon held its "Prime Big Deal Days" on Oct. 7 and 8. The reasoning is that global shopping events in the fourth quarter could serve as upward momentum for cosmetics shares.APR and Silicon2 are cited as the stocks most likely to lead a rebound. APR shares have been pressured by controversy over Sudan Red and a slide in its Amazon rankings, but the company's own testing found no trace of the substance in question, raising the possibility that counterfeit products were involved.The drop in Amazon rankings is also seen as a temporary effect of the end of Europe's "back to school" season. The number of APR products sold online at Ulta Beauty has risen from about 30 in July to roughly 50 now, and entry into Costco is expected to materialize in the second half.At Silicon2, gross margin is projected to rise from 30% in the first quarter to 31% in the third quarter as higher-margin sales through Boots and iHerb account for a larger share of revenue.
